card.name: Vimbuza
card.tagline: Tumbuka spirit-possession healing dance of northern Malawi
card.profile: Vimbuza is the spirit-possession healing dance of the Tumbuka people of northern Malawi (and eastern Zambia), a manifestation of the Bantu ng'oma ('drums of affliction') healing complex (UNESCO ICH; Wikipedia). Patients - most often women suffering mental illness - are treated over weeks or months by a healer running a temphiri (healing house); during the ritual, women and children form a circle and sing to call helping spirits while men beat spirit-specific drum rhythms, allowing the patient to enter trance and 'dance their disease' (kuvina nthenda) (UNESCO ICH). The ritual dates to the mid-19th century.
card.insight: Vimbuza developed partly as a way to process the trauma of oppression and survived suppression by Christian missionaries and a 1924 British ban; UNESCO proclaimed it a Masterpiece in 2005 and inscribed it on the Representative List in 2008 (UNESCO ICH; Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: A healing dance to 'dance the disease'. A representative image shows ceremonial regalia in a ritual context — imagery should be handled respectfully, not as spectacle — Tumbuka, Malawi.
